## 1. Executive summary

Summarize the supplied simulation you analyzed, the most important evidence-backed finding, the guard behaviour observed and the recovery result.

## 2. Scope, safety and method

Identify the assigned VM, the canonical source path (`labs/ot-security/student-lab-source/`), the loopback-only authorized scope, snapshot/recovery arrangement and confirmation that no real or external system was targeted. State the method used to collect evidence.

## 3. Supplied architecture and process model

Explain the supplied component roles and data flow using your annotated topology. Cite the source files you inspected. Include your verified register/data-point map; distinguish source-defined facts from assumptions.

## 4. Normal operations and packet evidence

Describe the observed normal process values and dashboard behaviour. Link the baseline to a learner-created capture, and explain a matching Modbus/TCP request/response and what it proves.

## 5. Local exposure and risk assessment

Summarize the documented loopback services, their process significance, material risks and proposed preventative/detective controls. Confirm that discovery stayed within the authorized source scope.

## 6. Supplied guard analysis

Explain the checks and decisions you verified in the provided guard, assumptions behind them, relevant event/log evidence and limitations. Separate implemented behaviours from recommendations; do not claim the guard provides comprehensive protection.

## 7. Controlled validation and findings

For each approved scenario, state the supplied script/path, starting state, expected outcome, observed result, supporting packet/log/dashboard evidence, interpretation and recovery outcome. Include an expected-versus-observed comparison table.

## 8. Recommendations

Recommend realistic improvements to monitoring, segmentation, authorization, resilience and operational process. Label these as recommendations, not features already present in the source.

## 9. Recovery and conclusion

State how processes were stopped, the approved state was verified/restored and what the lab demonstrates. Explain remaining limitations honestly.

## 10. References and appendices

Cite the course repository and exact source commit, relevant code files, approved external references, topology, register map, evidence log, risk register, test plan and evidence inventory. State clearly that the provided code is course source and not your original implementation.
